ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A train is accelerating on a straight track with an acceleration of $0.98\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. A passenger inside the train extends their hand out of the window and releases an object from a height of $2.5\mathrm{m}$ above the ground, neglecting air resistance. ($g$ is taken as $9.8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$)

1. What is the horizontal distance between the object and the passenger when the object hits the ground?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A train is accelerating on a straight track with an acceleration of $0.98\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. A passenger inside the train extends their hand out of the window and releases an object from a height of $2.5\mathrm{m}$ above the ground, neglecting air resistance. ($g$ is taken as $9.8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$) 1. What is the horizontal distance between the object and the passenger when the object hits the ground?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given from the text: train acceleration a = 0.98 m/s^2, release height h = 2.5 m, and g = 9.8 m/s^2; air resistance is neglected. The vertical motion determines the fall time: h = (1/2) g t^2, so t = sqrt(2h/g). Therefore t^2 = 2h/g = 2(2.5)/9.8. Horizontally, at the instant of release, the object and passenger have the same horizontal velocity. After release, the object has no horizontal acceleration, while the passenger continues accelerating with the train at a = 0.98 m/s^2. Thus the horizontal separation after time t is Δx = (1/2) a t^2. Substituting t^2 gives Δx = (1/2)a(2h/g) = ah/g = (0.98)(2.5)/9.8 = 0.25 m. Final answer: the object is 0.25 m behind the passenger when it hits the ground.
